newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Monday amid weak demand for funds due to the sluggish domestic stock market, traders said.
Many institutions kept to the sidelines despite relatively low rates following last week's slide, and traders linked this to the weak sentiment on the bourse.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 7.70 percent from 7.99 percent last Friday.
Total volume of the six-contract market fell to 2.45 million lots from 4.08 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said they expected contracts to move around current levels in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher on Monday with short-term funds flowing back to the spot market from the weak domestic stock markets, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in July 2006 rose to 113.41 yuan from 113.27 yuan. Combined volume of the eight contract market fell to 759,456 lots from 1.04 million lots.
Traders said spot contracts would rise slightly in the next few days on further consolidation on the A share market.
